purpose: Retrospective benchmark/protocol interpretation of already completed studies; not novelty search or full-paper review.

paper.title: Re-TACRED: Addressing Shortcomings of the TACRED Dataset

assertions.finding: Relation extraction predicts the relation from a sentence and designated subject/object spans.

assertions.locator: p2 dataset background and release footnote
assertions.finding: Original TACRED time-based splits and inherited source-data access are described. Public correction patches do not redistribute full source text.
Identity relations, organization membership/parent ambiguities and branch labels are corrected; these annotation changes do not certify later interventions as semantically invariant.
Final dataset has91467 examples and40 relation types, retaining original train/development/test allocation.

paper.limits: No full-paper, supplement, model-code, data-conversion or original-license-entitlement audit claimed. Page6 was only partially read and supplies no quantitative comparison here.

findings: README identifies91467-example pruned release asv1.1, versus105206-examplev1.0.
Reconstruction uses public label corrections plus separately obtained original TACRED source; raw source is not redistributed.
These repository facts do not alone prove this project conversion was generated from that exact upstream patch.

scorer.read_scope: score() label-accounting branches and final micro aggregation; no training code executed.
scorer.finding: Non-no_relation true positives, guessed positives and gold positives define benchmark micro-F1. Project full40 Macro-F1 is a different declared metric.
scorer.limits: Degenerate zero-guessed-positive precision convention differs (upstream defaults1, project0); F1 remains0. Existing25 test cells have positive denominators. No claim of general scorer-byte equivalence.
